title: Review of c52's digestion ecology on fresh seed 4 (256^2): both kinds divide (predators 40 persistent splits, generation 3; prey 62, generation 4) and predators die when the prey are removed (43 -> 0 within 900 t, fed twin 47); predators sit as comets on prey (86% touch prey, 16% of their area inside)
summary: labkit run of the claim's world.py (defaults, K=20) on seed 4 at 256^2 to t=12000, and at 128^2 the predator-starvation fork (dfork_t 6000: all prey material removed) against its fed twin. 256^2: prey 191 bodies at the end, 62 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 0.48; predators 189 bodies, 87 persistent tracks, 40 persistent splits, generation 3, merge/split 0.34. onprey.py over t >= 2000: 86% of predator bodies (c_b > 0.5, >= 4 px) touch prey, 16% of their area lies inside prey, 26 free predators per frame. Fork: predator bodies 43 (t=5800) -> 35 (t=6300) -> 4 (t=6600) -> 0 (t=6900); fed twin 43 -> 47.

observations.S: rerun256/sheet.png t=0 unstructured prey field; predators from noise added at t=2000
observations.I: predators are separate comet-shaped bodies with only 16% of their area inside prey and 26 free per frame (onprey.py), 87 persistent predator tracks
observations.D: predators 40 persistent splits, generation 3; prey 62, generation 4 (rerun256 FACTS species lines)
observations.E: dfork128 vs fed128: predators 43 -> 0 by t=6900 after the prey are removed, fed twin 47; the predator material is conserved and never made from prey, so this dependence is dynamical

verdicts.limitation: X not checked (no predator-free twin run here; the author's twins are frozen emulsions). Predator divisions are mostly joint with prey divisions (the predator is drawn out between two prey daughters), and 86% of predators touch prey, so the predator is a free body only part of the time. The fork is at 128^2 and one seed; prey-side fuel fork not rerun. Merge/split 0.48 for prey is near the reticulate cap.
